title: railyard-symbols 0.3.3
description: A symbols file: source positions, and for each its links back to the artifacts that caused it. One index document describes a directory; one version document describes what changed at one version. A reader ignores any field it does not know, and refuses a formatVersion it does not know: while the major version is 0, its minor version is the compatibility unit. MIT-licensed.

root.description: The path from this directory to the root of the tree the file paths are relative to: POSIX, relative, and ".." for a directory sitting in that root. It is how a symbols directory names the tree it describes, needing no git, no remote URL and no configuration. A reader given no root of its own resolves positions against this one.

files.description: Every path any version names, relative to the root of the tree the positions are in. Referred to by its place in this list.

artifacts.description: Every artifact any version links to. Referred to by its place in this list.

commits.description: Every commit any version names: a version's own, an artifact's version, or the commit a link was made in. Referred to by its place in this list.

links.description: Every distinct link any version carries, written once for the directory. A position names its links by their place in this list, so a link true of many positions is not repeated at each of them.

versions.description: The versions this directory holds, each a delta against the one it names as its base, oldest first.

commit.description: The commit this version describes, in full, so that the file stands alone. It must be the commit the index names for it.

base.description: The commit of the version this one is a delta against; null for the first version.

files.description: The positions of each file that changed since the base, each file restated whole. The key is the file's place in the index's files list, in decimal.

removed.description: The files whose positions are gone at this version, by their place in the index's files list.

commit.description: The version's commit, by its place in the index's commits list.

base.description: The version this one is a delta against, by its place in the versions list; it is always an earlier entry. Null for the first version.

file.description: The version's own file, relative to the directory holding index.json.

builds.description: The build hashes this version answers for: the value dev.railyard.build-hash carries in each build made from this version. A version may answer for several, since one commit can be built more than one way. No two versions may name the same hash.

position.description: A range of a file, and its links back. The start is inclusive and the end exclusive, read as a pair (line, column): a whole line L of n characters is [L, 1] to [L, n + 1]. A range whose start equals its end covers exactly that one position, which is how an empty line is covered. Lines and columns are 1-based.

at.description: [start line, start column, end line, end column].

names.description: What this position NAMES: the function, class, method or binding its first line falls inside. A position held by a file and a line is destroyed by an edit anywhere above it; one that names the thing it is in survives an edit above it, a reformat and a move within the file, which is what an anchor is for. Absent where nothing names the position — a comment, an import, a top-level constant — and absent is honest: a wrong name is worse than none, because a reader believes it. Producers are not required to emit it, and a consumer that has it should prefer it to the line numbers.

links.description: This position's links, by their place in the index's links list.

link.description: One artifact this position traces to, and how that is known.

artifact.description: The artifact, by its place in the index's artifacts list.

evidence.description: How the link is known. recorded: recorded when the code was made. cited: cited in the code, a commit message or another document. tested: shown by a criterion's tests running this position. confirmed: proposed, and confirmed by a person. A cited or inferred link is never shown as verified.

source.description: The concrete source the link was read from. A producer may use a name of its own; readers show it as written.

state.description: current: the artifact has not changed since the link was made. suspect: it has, or it did not exist then, so the link waits to be confirmed again. missing: the artifact is not there at the version's commit.

linked.description: The artifact's own version when the link was made, by its place in the index's commits list; null when the artifact did not exist then.

current.description: The artifact's own version at this version's commit, by its place in the index's commits list; null when it is missing.

linkedContent.description: A hash of the artifact's own content at `linked` — the criterion's text, not the file's. The WITNESS, where the id and the commit are the address: comparing it against `currentContent` says whether the artifact moved under this link, with no repository, network or walk through history, which is what makes the question askable of a deployed build and askable of every link at once. Absent on a link written before this was carried; absent means 'cannot compare', never 'unchanged'.

currentContent.description: A hash of the artifact's own content at `current`, on the same terms as `linkedContent`.

madeBy.description: Where the link was made: a commit, and the file and line it is written in when it is written in one.

commit.description: By its place in the index's commits list.

path.description: By its place in the index's files list; null when the link is not written in a file.

artifact.description: An artifact a position traces to: a specification, one of its criteria, a decision record, an architecture model's node, or anything else a producer's adapter names. Nothing here belongs to a language, a framework or a build tool.

kind.description: The artifact's kind, as the producer's adapter names it.

path.description: The artifact's document, relative to the root of the tree.

anchor.description: The part of that document the artifact is, such as one criterion or one node; null for the whole document.

label.description: How people READ it. Display only: a reader that stores this as the reference has stored a name that moves.

id.description: The artifact's stable ID, where it declares one: characters set when the artifact is created and never changed. THIS is the reference. `path`, `anchor` and `label` all move when a document is renamed or a part of it renumbered, and this does not, so a link held by it survives what a link held by position does not. Absent where the artifact declares no stable ID.

commit.description: A commit, with its committer date and time for people to read. The pair of a stable id and a commit is how an artifact version is referred to.

buildHash.description: A build's hash: the value dev.railyard.build-hash carries. A SHA-256 over the build's own content, as 64 lowercase hex characters.
